newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Autoliv, Morton link to create airbag giant.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Autoliv, Morton link to create airbag giant.

text.p: Swedish car safety group Autoliv announced on Monday plans to create the world's largest airbag manufacturer through a merger with the automotive safety division of U.S.-based Morton International.
The new company, to be known as Autoliv Inc, will have an annual turnover of 20 billion crowns ($3.01 billion), 15,000 employees and will operate on a global scale.

"The planned deal fits in perfectly with our strategy of attempting to strengthen Autoliv's position in the U.S. and Japan, where Morton's (car safety unit) ASP already has a strong position," Autoliv president Paul Charlety said in a statement.
Shares in Autoliv soared as the Stockholm bourse opened, the stock gaining 51 crowns or 21 percent to 305 crowns in the first five minutes of trading.
Although the Swedish company's turnover of $1.5 billion is slightly greater than that of Mortons ASP, Autoliv spokesman Mats Odman said his company had the most to gain in terms of profitability.
"You can't ignore the fact that Morton earned $256 million on its airbags (in 1995). They've got an operating margin of 18 percent, whilst we have nine percent," he said.
"In the long term the merger will provide synergies but you can't expect to pay off from day one...in time it will mean more profits for Autoliv's shareholders," Odman added.
The head office of the new company will be in either Amsterdam or London, Autoliv said, but its legal domicile will be in the United States. Shares will be listed in New York and Stockholm.

The deal will be a "merger of equals", under which Autoliv AB's owners will exchange their interest for 53.5 percent of the shares in Autoliv Inc, and shareholders in Morton International will swap ASP for 46.5 percent of the shares in the new company.
The board of Autoliv Inc will initially consist of equal numbers from Autoliv AB and Morton International.

However, Gunnar Bark, who was Autoliv's chief executive until last month, will become chairman of the board. Fred Musone, currently president of Mortons ASP, will be chief executive of the new company while Paul Charlety will become chief operating officer.
Immediately prior to the merger, Morton International will transfer its salt and specialty chemicals division to a new company which will take over the name Morton International.
The new company will also receive a capital injection of $750 million, financed via new borrowing within ASP. The sum will thus become a liability within the Autoliv Inc group.
Morton International chairman S Jay Stewart said the funds would be used for acquisitions and buy-backs of own shares after the completion of the merger.

The signing of the final agreement, which Autoliv said was expected to take place within six weeks, requires a satisfactory due diligence investigation and the approval of the boards of both companies.
It will also require the approval of the majority of Morton International's shareholders as well as 90 percent of the shareholders in Autoliv AB. ($1=6.653 Swedish Crown)
